nodes.name: H2O2 Etching for Oxygen Defects
nodes.procedure: Oxygen defects were introduced into NiFe-LDH grown on nickel foam through controlled H2O2 etching using 160 μL H2O2 (optimal among 0, 80, 120, 160, and 200 μL), confirmed by EPR signal at g=2.003 and O 1s XPS showing 62.49% oxygen defects.
nodes.source_text: by first introducing oxygen defects into NiFe-LDH through controlled H2O2 etching (0, 80, 120, 160, and 200 μL), followed by precise regulation of PtCl4 solution concentration... optimal sample... using 160 μL H2O2.

nodes.name: Pt Loading on D-NiFe-LDH
nodes.procedure: Atomically dispersed Pt atoms (0.38, 1.08, 1.27, 3.83 wt.% loadings confirmed by ICP) were anchored onto oxygen-deficient D-NiFe-LDH through precise regulation of PtCl4 solution concentration via two-step hydrothermal method, achieving optimal Pt/D-NiFe-LDH with 1.27 wt.% Pt loading.
nodes.source_text: The synthesis of atomically dispersed Pt atoms on oxygen-deficient NiFe-LDH (D-NiFe-LDH) was achieved through a two-step hydrothermal method... systematically prepared samples with varying Pt loadings (0.38, 1.08, 1.27, and 3.83 wt.%)... optimal sample, designated as Pt/D-NiFe-LDH, contained 1.27 wt.% Pt.

nodes.characterization_summary: Isolated bright spots confirm atomic dispersion of Pt species with lattice fringes 1.53 Å and 2.66 Å matching (110) and (101) planes of D-NiFe-LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As can be seen from the spherical aberration-corrected high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (AC-HAADF-STEM) plots (Figure 1c; Figure S6, Supporting Information) of the samples, the lattice fringes 1.53Å and 2.66Å within them match the (110) and (101) crystallographic planes of D-NiFe-LDH, respectively. The presence of isolated bright spots confirms the atomic dispersion of Pt species.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt/D-NiFe-LDH shows interconnected standing nanosheet morphology with nanopores; Pt loading preserves nanosheet structure with thinner sheets and larger nanopores.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As depicted in Figure 1b, Pt/D-NiFe-LDH has an interconnected standing nanosheet morphology, with a large number of nanopores between these nanosheets.

properties.description: Gray-scale TEM/SEM image showing nanoparticle morphology

nodes.characterization_summary: Uniform dispersion of Ni, Fe, O throughout Pt/D-NiFe-LDH with atomically dispersed Pt atoms across the framework.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1d illustrates the elemental distribution within the sample, revealing uniform dispersion of Ni, Fe, and O throughout the material. Additionally, Pt atoms are atomically dispersed across the D-NiFe-LDH framework.

nodes.characterization_summary: Characteristic peaks of NiFe-LDH at 11.60°, 23.39°, 33.73°, 34.48°, 38.94°, 46.39°, 59.89°, 61.17°; no Pt-related peaks confirm atomic dispersion; (110) peak shifts to higher angles with oxygen defects, (003) peak shifts to lower angle after Pt loading.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis of powdered samples reveals characteristic peaks corresponding to the (003), (006), (101), (012), (015), (018), (110), and (113) planes of NiFe-LDH (JCPDS No. 40-0215) at 11.60°, 23.39°, 33.73°, 34.48°, 38.94°, 46.39°, 59.89°, and 61.17°, respectively (Figure 1e).

nodes.characterization_summary: Distinct signal at g = 2.003 characteristic of oxygen defects; concentration significantly increased after H2O2 addition.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy reveals a distinct signal at g = 2.003 (Figure 1f), characteristic of oxygen defects.

nodes.characterization_summary: Peaks at 310 cm⁻¹ (e_g bending NiO-H), 462 cm⁻¹ (tensile Ni-O a1g), 528 cm⁻¹ (e_g bending Ni-OH); 528 cm⁻¹ peak disappears and 462 cm⁻¹ red shifts in Pt-loaded sample indicating strong Pt-NiFe-LDH interaction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1g presents the Raman spectra of the samples. The e_g bending of NiO-H is responsible for the peak at 310 cm⁻¹. The tensile vibration of Ni-O a1g and the e_g bending of Ni-OH are responsible for the two peaks at 462 cm⁻¹ and 528 cm⁻¹, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt 4f XPS: Pt 4f7/2 at 70.60 eV and 4f5/2 at 74.02 eV (-0.80 eV shift vs Pt metal 71.40 eV) indicate negative valence state; Ni 2p3/2 shifts from 856.20 eV (NiFe-LDH) to 856.36 eV (Pt/NiFe-LDH) and 857.11 eV (Pt/D-NiFe-LDH); O 1s oxygen vacancy percentage 62.49% in Pt/D-NiFe-LDH vs 40.22% in Pt/NiFe-LDH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For Pt/D-NiFe-LDH, the 4f7/2 and 4f5/2 electrons of Pt are responsible for the peaks at 70.60 and 74.02 eV, respectively. Compared with the binding energy of 71.40 eV for the 4f7/2 electron of metal Pt, the above binding energy values indicate that Pt in Pt/D-NiFe-LDH is in a negative valence state. ... In comparison with Pt/NiFe-LDH, the percentage of oxygen defects in Pt/D-NiFe-LDH rises from 40.22% to 62.49%, confirming prior EPR data.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt L3-edge white line intensity lower than Pt foil, more pronounced for Pt/D-NiFe-LDH confirming stronger negative valence state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The samples' Pt L3-edge X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectra are displayed in Figure 2d. ... However, the Pt/D-NiFe-LDH white line peak's intensity is noticeably lower.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS peak at 2.70 Å corresponds to Pt-Ni(Fe) bonds (not Pt-Pt); wavelet transform confirms Pt-Ni(Fe) as main coordination environment.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2e exhibits a distinct peak at 2.70Å, which differs from the characteristic peak position of Pt-Pt bonds. Instead, this peak position aligns well with the reported Pt-Ni bond distance in the literature.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt loadings confirmed as 0.38, 1.08, 1.27, and 3.83 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma analysis confirms the Pt loadings (Figure S1, Supporting Information)

nodes.characterization_summary: Cdl values: Pt/D-NiFe-LDH 8.40 mF cm⁻² (1M KOH), 10.24 mF cm⁻² (1M KPi) indicating highest ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Cdl values for these catalysts are 0.57, 1.10, 5.84, 8.40, and 6.27 mF cm⁻², respectively (Figure S13, Supporting Information). ... The Cdl values for these catalysts are 0.87, 1.25, 6.25, 10.24, and 4.57 mF cm⁻², respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt/D-NiFe-LDH shows lowest charge transfer resistance among tested catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) experiments demonstrate Pt/D-NiFe-LDH possesses a lower charge transfer resistance than the other catalysts (Figure S16, Supporting Information)
